FLOODLIT AFTER DARK

Same football energy as the last pass, completely different world. Nobody plays at midday in Dubai — so the whole app lives at 9pm under the lights.

Black-green turf with mown stripes, one electric lime that behaves like a floodlight, sodium amber and kit pink alongside it. Broadcast-wide Archivo for every number, Sora for everything else. Light does the work: glow instead of drop shadows, no emoji, no toy edges.

WHAT TO TRY

Screen 2 — the teams are laid out on a floodlit pitch. You are the pink 8, glowing.

Screen 4 — sparks at full time, then vote man of the match and watch the card light up.

Screen 3 — "I can't make it" → "Pass my shirt on". A spinning ball under a floodlight beam, then your money back on a lime card. Still the whole argument against CeleBreak's forfeited credits.

THE BITS THAT BRING PEOPLE BACK

The player card is a holo trading card — gradient edge, shirt-number watermark, goals and streak. Built to be screenshotted into a group chat, which is free marketing.

The season table glows on your row and remembers you have beaten Marco four times out of six. Bragging rights are the product.

THE RULES

Lime is the action and nothing else may use it. Pink is you. Amber is a warning or a draw.

Depth comes from light, never from drop shadows — a glow tightens around whatever you can press, and turf is always striped and lit from one end.

Motion is spent on winning, scoring and getting your money back. Nowhere else moves.
